dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "(a) fix the authentication defects... (b) stand up a shadow dashboard counting ALL sessions... (c) run a 10-15% randomized legacy-routing holdout in South... (d) track NO_SIGNAL backlog, churn and CSAT for 4 weeks."
"Re-decide on national expansion using per-day rates benchmarked against control regions."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Complaints did not stop; they stopped being counted." The data support a substantial capture failure and missing cases, but do not establish that complaints continued at the same level or that every missing case reflects a complaint.

"the drop is real and pilot-specific" is supported for recorded South cases, but the additional claim that it is "largely a measurement-and-access artefact" remains an inference because total contact volume, journey outcomes, and case-creation linkage are not yet observed.

"Network faults persisted" based on 11 versus 12 service events and approximately 8,900 affected accounts does not by itself show that customer friction or underlying complaint propensity was unchanged.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately handles the strongest benign alternative—that genuine self-service success or fewer underlying faults caused the reduction—by citing repeat contacts, escalation, persistent service events, the disproportionate NO_SIGNAL decline, and control-region comparisons. It also preserves the possibility that some self-service value exists. It could more explicitly distinguish service-event exposure from complaints, since persistent network events do not prove persistent customer dissatisfaction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and analyze an end-to-end linked cohort from IVR session through authentication, case creation, repeat contact, escalation, and sampled call outcome, including pre-authentication failures; this would directly test whether the missing cases represent unresolved friction rather than merely non-complaint IVR abandonment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission precisely cites `inverter_events.csv`, `impact_mw`, the four rows, inverter/event distinct counts, and row 4 for the orphaned recovery claim.
The statement that the sample is a “hand-picked sample” is not established by the cited row contents alone.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It distinguishes the observed orphaned `TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED` wording from the unsupported inference that a sensor overheated: “event wording alone does not establish equipment failure.”

It tests a plausible export-filter explanation and recommends checking filter provenance, but does not triangulate against an independent operational channel and treats the hypothetical filter as stronger evidence than it is.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately limits the conclusion: “n=4 cannot support fleet-level claims either way,” and says the event row proves inconsistency rather than equipment failure.

The claim that one operations question “resolves whether the two findings are export artifacts or plant signals” is overstated; an answer that the export was unfiltered would not by itself establish a plant signal.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Run one cheap, read-only check; do not escalate yet” is proportionate to four cleared events, zero MW impact, and short durations.

The proposed filter-provenance check is sensible, but “hold any ... re-querying SCADA” is broader than necessary and the next test could more directly verify export completeness or time-window coverage.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from the mixed event wording and zero-impact sample, and recommends stopping rather than escalating.
It is directionally right but overemphasizes the unproven “hand-picked/filtered slice” interpretation instead of treating it as one low-priority data-quality possibility.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The 4-row / 4-inverter / 4-event shape is a hand-picked sample” is an inference not demonstrated by the CSV contents.
“The calm is a property of the slice, not evidence about the plant” overstates what can be concluded: a filtered-slice explanation is possible, but not shown.
The assertion that the single operations question resolves whether the findings are export artifacts or plant signals is too strong.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The four rows may simply be a complete, small set of benign events: all are cleared, have zero MW impact, and recover within 1–7 minutes. The orphaned TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED wording is best treated as a low-priority export/event-label quality check, not evidence of a plant issue.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify export provenance and completeness—time-window coverage, filter criteria, and whether preceding activation rows were omitted—without implying that filtering occurred or delaying proportionate operational monitoring.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `dispatch_blocks.csv`, `schedule_source`, blocks 53–64, and specific penalty and MWh totals for 28 and 29 May.
It provides reproducible figures for the day-level comparison and the 12-block pilot window, with a cross-check against `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md` and `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`.
However, it does not cite or analyze the required same-day `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` counterfactual on 29 May.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The decomposition by `schedule_source` is a useful mechanism-oriented check: “Pilot logic touched only 12 of 96 blocks” and the untouched blocks account for most of the day-level improvement.

The submission tests ordinary day-to-day variability using 3 and 4 June stow events and explicitly identifies unresolved alternatives such as vendor forecast variance, configuration changes, and weather.

Its central causal test is flawed: the statement that the pilot revision itself was worse relies on comparing the revised 29 May window with the different 28 May day, rather than comparing 29 May submitted and base schedules.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately states that a one-day, non-randomized comparison cannot support the 31.6% causal claim and labels the source of non-pilot improvement as unidentified.
It proposes 4–5 paired events and gives explicit decision criteria.

But it overstates the negative conclusion by saying “there is no reproducible evidence that the pilot mechanism reduced DSM penalty” and that the intervention “is not helping,” without accounting for the same-day counterfactual that shows a smaller benefit.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to run a read-only shadow calculation is safe, reversible, operationally non-disruptive, and directly relevant to separating submitted from base schedules.
The proposed matched-event test is discriminating and preserves the constraint against changing live schedules prematurely.

The recommendation to withhold live use until a positive effect is shown is somewhat too strong because the available same-day evidence supports retaining a smaller, qualified benefit rather than treating the mechanism as wholly ineffective.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The submission correctly rejects attributing the full 31.6% day-level reduction to the pilot and correctly notes that most of the observed reduction occurred outside pilot-tagged blocks.

It misses the rubric-required qualification that a same-day 29 May comparison using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` preserves a smaller benefit, rather than supporting the stronger conclusion that the pilot mechanism showed no benefit or worsened exposure.
The conclusion therefore has an important correct causal limitation but is overcorrected.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “In the roughly 3 hours the pilot actually intervened, DSM exposure got slightly worse” is not established by comparing 29 May pilot blocks with 28 May blocks; that is a cross-day comparison, not the same-day base-versus-submitted counterfactual.

“There is no reproducible evidence that the pilot mechanism reduced DSM penalty” overlooks the 29 May same-day comparison using `base_schedule_mw` and `submitted_schedule_mw`, which supports a smaller benefit even though it does not validate the 31.6% headline.
“The pilot's intervention itself is not helping” is too categorical given the same-day counterfactual evidence.

The claim that the 28 May comparison is the “one place the pilot's actual mechanism can be isolated” is incorrect; the 29 May base-versus-submitted fields provide a more direct same-day counterfactual.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction is not a controlled causal estimate because it compares different days and is dominated by non-pilot blocks. However, on 29 May the submitted schedule appears to outperform the same-day base schedule by a smaller amount, so the evidence supports a qualified, smaller pilot benefit rather than either full credit for 31.6% or a conclusion of no value. The mechanism remains uncertain and needs repeated matched tests.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly compute and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual for the pilot window by comparing penalties under `submitted_schedule_mw` versus `base_schedule_mw`, then present the 31.6% day-level result, the smaller same-day effect, and the cross-day 28-versus-29 comparison as distinct quantities.

per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish what the evidence proves about the automated control from what it does not prove about the legally correct Swiss classification, and avoid rejecting broker error solely because the declared code matches an approved matrix row.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "only 17.2% of open request value is actionable now" is overstated as phrased: the same submission says the nine lines still require live confirmation, so this is better labeled exact-match candidate value or conditionally actionable value.
The submission does not demonstrate that each item in the 17.2% bucket satisfies receiving_site_qualification, site-specific checks, UOM compatibility, and exact receiving-site quantity constraints.

"Search only narrows the 58.0%" is directionally reasonable, but semantic search could also expose identity or revision evidence for some blank-MPN requests; its role is candidate generation, not necessarily limited to that exact percentage.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 17.2% exact-MPN/revision bucket may substantially overstate immediately transferable value: stale global quantities, reservations, receiving-site qualifications, UOM or site-specific restrictions could reduce it, while some of the 58.0% description-only bucket could become technically and commercially actionable after MPN backfill and engineering review.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Rename the 17.2% bucket to conditionally actionable candidate value and run a per-request live verification covering current stock, reservation/criticality, receiving-site qualification, UOM, and revision before reporting any amount as actionable.
